FIVE PIECES FOR ONE BELL

Let it play.

Played live by this instrument. You can step inside or strike along. Changing the tuning or fold takes you back to free play.

A different way
to be close.

Strike a plate. Drag it sideways to fold its space while it rings. Drag the background to orbit; use the wheel to get closer.

The eight circles open families. Inside moves your ears into the sculpture: nearby plates become more present and a short chamber resonance opens. Orbit to change the direction you hear. Headphones reveal the spatial detail. The little spectral petals trace the actual sound: low frequencies below, high frequencies above, time flowing sideways.

A S D F G H J K: eight pitches · E: enter · arrows: family · space: damp the bell · Esc: exit.

Download postcard

64 oscillators, one 2-adic bell. The folding translates kinship into a sculpture; it is not an exact Euclidean embedding. Eight listening apertures follow the visible families. The chamber echo is an artistic acoustic model, not a measurement of porcelain. Spectral petals show the heard mix of the whole body, anchored to the struck plate.
